raw_response:
I will keep the full 10.1 mu in my usual wheat-maize rotation, because I know this system well and I have well irrigation, so I can still aim for steady grain output without taking on extra crop risk. I am not going to chase the very highest demonstration-field yield. At my age, with only two people in the household, I would rather use a simpler, steadier plan that I can manage myself. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put most of the phosphorus and potassium in at seeding, keep nitrogen moderate, and irrigate at the key times instead of watering too often. I will do a plough-based seedbed before wheat this year because local guidance still stresses periodic deep tillage to break the hardpan, and I want better rooting. For maize, I will follow right after wheat harvest, use hybrid seed, keep fertilizer balanced but not excessive, and use no-tillage so I can sow fast and save labor. I will plan a small number of pesticide applications on both crops, because I want to control the main disease and insect risks without overspending. My yield target is below the top Quzhou demonstration fields, but high enough to make the land worth farming.
